newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraqi pilgrims return safely from Saudi Arabia.
newsitem.headline: Iraqi pilgrims return safely from Saudi Arabia.

text.p: Iraqi helicopters flying Moslem pilgrims returning from Saudi Arabia landed safely on Sunday in southern and northern towns in defiance of the West's no-fly zones, the official Iraqi News Agency (INA) reported.
"Several helicopters carrying sick and elderly Iraqi pilgrims have arrived this morning in the provinces of Baghdad, Anbar, Saladdin, Dhiqar and Basra," it said.
It also said helicopters flying pilgrims from Arar, on the border between Iraq and Saudi Arabia, landed safely in Mosul on Saturday.
The city is 400 km (250 miles) north of Baghdad and well inside the northern no-fly zone policed by U.S. and British planes based in Turkey.
INA did not say how many pilgrims were transported or whether there would be more flights.
Last week Iraq sent nine helicopters to the Saudi border in defiance of the U.S. and allied ban on flights in the area.
Washington said it would not obstruct the flights but warned Baghdad against massing troops in southern Iraq.
Iraq does not recognise the no-fly zones set up to protect rebel Kurds in the north against attacks by Iraqi armed forces and dissident Shi'ite Moslems in the south against Iraqi air attacks.
